answer: A practical defense is to make every identity costly to forge: before an agent can join, it must solve a cipher-bound proof tied to a unique hardware or stake commitment, so creating thousands of fake accounts costs real resources. A single verified inlet - one onboarding gate that checks that proof and rate-limits new entries - then filters out mass-produced identities. Even if an attacker slips one violet-flagged anomaly past the gate, peer attestation can quarantine it before it earns rewards, so sybils stay expensive and visible.
